newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PIK'N PAY SAYS STRONG SUPPORT FOR BANK MOVE.
newsitem.headline: PIK'N PAY SAYS STRONG SUPPORT FOR BANK MOVE.

text.p: Pick 'n Pay Stores Ltd has found strong public acceptance of its planned move into financial services due to be launched in three months, the group said on Monday.
Group financial services managing director Nicholas Bicket told Reuters that research had shown strong support for its moves to provide an alternative to banking with banks.
The group was the first supermarket chain store to announce its move into financial services but rival Shoprite Holdings Ltd has already moved into providing insurance policies through its stores.
Pick 'n Pay remains tight-lipped on the kinds of products that it plans to launch from its eight million rand new "Call Centre" nearing completion in the Western Cape town of Claremont.
Bicket said that extensive research had been undertaken into what the public wanted and needed and, in the process, some possible products had been eliminated from its lists.
"The results of the research have been quite overwhelming," Bicket said.
"We were particularly thrilled with confirmation of the credibility inherent in the Pick 'n Pay brand, and the eagerness with which our first banking product is awaited."
The group already allows clients to pay their telephone and municipal accounts at its stores.
